question: Catalonia is suffering the worst period of drought since records began. Rainfall in 2023 was 30-50 % lower than the year-on-year average of the last three decades. Many municipalities are suffering water cuts for up to fourteen hours a day and their councils have had to pay to source alternative water resources. The Catalan Government plans to reduce tap pressure for six million people or to bring in water by boat.

Water bills will rise by 11.5 % and losses in the agricultural sector will be to the tune of EUR 700 million. Rural areas are particularly worried about this current drought, as rice production is expected to fall by more than 20 % compared to the last four years, and oil production by more than 12 000 tonnes. In light of this: 1.
What mechanisms does the Commission have at its disposal to counter the drought which is affecting rural areas in Catalonia and their crops?
What compensatory aid could Catalan businesses affected by the drought in rural areas be eligible for?
What measures does the Commission think the Catalan Government or the Spanish Government should adopt to compensate for the economic damage caused by the drought?
answer: 1. The new Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) promotes a sustainable and resilient agricultural sector to ensure food security, and fosters and supports strategies for environmental protection and climate action.

The CAP Strategic Plans 2023-2027 (CSPs) contain a range of instruments to support adaptation to climate change and preventive action, to deal with water management challenges and support a transition to more water resilient agriculture given the increasing water shortages and more severe droughts. CSPs can also support risk management measures to better shield food production against risks of drought.

EU funding to promote more sustainable water management in Spain is also available through the European Regional Development Fund. For the period 2021-2027 the Programme for Catalonia allocated EUR 70 million to support the regeneration and reuse of wastewater and the reduction of water leakages. 2.

To compensate Spanish farmers affected by the drought and other adverse weather events, the Commission adopted in July 2023 an emergency support package, funded through the 2023 agricultural reserve (1). Spain benefitted with EUR 81 million. The Spanish authorities decided how to distribute the amount amongst the sectors most in need.

The EU funding available and the national plans provide a broad range of tools to assist Member States and local communities to respond and adapt to the consequences of adverse weather events such as the drought in Spain, in all agricultural sectors including cereals and oilseeds. 3.

In the case of adverse climatic events which can be assimilated to a natural disaster, the national authorities may also grant, under certain conditions, support to farmers from their national budget in line with EU State aid rules (2).
